sources.entry: egroupware - Software suite including calendars, address books, notepad, project management tools, client relationship management tools (CRM), knowledge management tools, a wiki and a CMS. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: EGroupware is a groupware software suite covering calendars, address books, notepad, project management, CRM, knowledge management, a wiki and a CMS.
summary.what_it_does: The README is short and mostly covers installation rather than features; the feature list comes from the awesome-selfhosted listing metadata (calendars, address books, notepad, project management, CRM, knowledge management, wiki, CMS). It recommends installing via the Linux distribution package manager, with instructions in the project wiki and distribution-specific guides. For non-Linux systems or unsupported distributions, EGroupware 26 can be run in Docker, and the DEB/RPM packages also use Docker internally. The development version is recommended to be installed via Docker because it includes a push-server container. The README also describes a deprecated developer install from a git clone using composer, npm and an install-cli.php script. The install-cli.php script also handles updates and switching between channels: release (tagged maintenance releases), bugfix (release branch), a named branch, or master (latest development).
how_to_run: Install EGroupware via your Linux distribution package manager (see the wiki for instructions)
Docker: follow the instructions in the wiki or the doc/docker subdirectory of the repository
Run setup/setup-cli.php after updating to check whether a schema update is needed
notable: Preferred installation is through Linux distribution packages (DEB/RPM), which run EGroupware in Docker internally
Development version via Docker includes a push-server container
install-cli.php manages update channels: release, bugfix, named branch, and master
caveats: The README says the non-package install methods, including a developer clone, are more complicated and lack some features, because parts run in separate containers such as the push-server
The git-clone developer installation is marked deprecated in the README
Detailed installation steps are in an external wiki, not in the README
